==============================
 Function: read_input (0x400886)
==============================
Reads user input via read(0, buf, size).
If read returns <= 0, prints "Error" and calls _exit(-1).

  read_input(char *buf, size_t size):
    n = read(0, buf, size)
    if (n <= 0) { puts("Error"); _exit(-1); }

Prints the Easy Heap Creator banner and menu options:

==============================
 Function: create_heap (0x400931)
==============================
  create_heap():
    for (i = 0; i <= 9; i++):
      if (heaparray[i] == NULL):
        printf("Size of Heap : ")
        read(0, &size, 8)
        size = atoi(&size)
        heaparray[i] = malloc(size)
        if (heaparray[i] == NULL):
          puts("Allocate Error")
          exit(2)
        printf("Content of heap:")
        read_input(heaparray[i], size)    ← reads exactly 'size' bytes
        puts("SuccessFul")
        break

==============================
 Function: edit_heap (0x400a47) — VULNERABLE
==============================
  edit_heap():
    printf("Index :")
    read(0, &index, 4)
    index = atoi(&index)
    if (index < 0 || index > 9):
      puts("Out of bound!")
      exit(0)
    if (heaparray[index] == NULL):
      puts("No such heap !")
      return
    printf("Size of Heap : ")
    read(0, &new_size, 8)
    new_size = atoi(&new_size)        ← USER CONTROLS NEW SIZE!
    printf("Content of heap : ")
    read_input(heaparray[index], new_size)  ← HEAP OVERFLOW!
    puts("Done !")

⚠️ VULNERABILITY: edit_heap reads a NEW size from the user and passes it to
   read_input() for an EXISTING heap chunk. If new_size > original malloc size,
   the write overflows into adjacent heap chunks. No bounds check whatsoever.

==============================
 Function: delete_heap (0x400b53)
==============================
  delete_heap():
    printf("Index :")
    read(0, &index, 4)
    index = atoi(&index)
    if (index < 0 || index > 9):
      puts("Out of bound!")
      exit(0)
    if (heaparray[index] == NULL):
      puts("No such heap !")
      return
    free(heaparray[index])
    heaparray[index] = NULL            ← CORRECTLY NULLIFIED (no UAF)
    puts("Done !")

✓ delete_heap properly sets pointer to NULL after free. No Use-After-Free.

==============================
 Function: l33t (0x400c23) — Backdoor
==============================
  l33t():
    system("cat /home/pwn/flag")

⚠️ NOTE: The flag file path "/home/pwn/flag" does NOT exist on the remote server.
   The actual flag is at "/flag". This means triggering l33t() alone is insufficient.
   We need a shell to read /flag.

==============================
 Function: main (0x400c34)
==============================
  main():
    setvbuf(stdout, 0, 2, 0)     ← unbuffered
    setvbuf(stdin, 0, 2, 0)      ← unbuffered
    menu()
    while (1):
      printf("Your choice :")
      read(0, &choice, 8)
      choice = atoi(&choice)
      switch (choice):
        case 1: create_heap(); break
        case 2: edit_heap(); break
        case 3: delete_heap(); break
        case 4: exit(0)
        case 0x1305 (4869):       ← HIDDEN BACKDOOR TRIGGER
          if (magic > 0x1305):
            puts("Congrt !")
            l33t()                ← calls system("cat /home/pwn/flag")
          else:
            puts("So sad !")
          break
        default: puts("Invalid Choice")

⚠️ Hidden feature: Inputting 4869 (0x1305) as menu choice checks if the BSS
   variable 'magic' (at 0x6020c0) is greater than 0x1305. If so, calls l33t().
